title: When the Parish Falls
premise: Estate lawyer Ivo Fairweather is hired by a nervous parishioner to prove that a murder predicted in a sealed will — dated three days in the future — will not happen at the vicar's anniversary dinner. As Ivo traces the will's impossible provenance, he discovers the document was drafted by his own late mentor, implicating the parish family that once gave him a sense of belonging. Torn between loyalty to the people who raised him and the truth the file demands, Ivo stages the dinner as a trap, forcing the killer — the vicar's own daughter, protecting a decades-old secret — to strike early and confess. The case closes, but Ivo loses the only home he ever had, choosing truth over belonging.
about_author: U. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former rural solicitor who spent twenty years drafting wills in English market towns before turning to crime fiction. They write mysteries steeped in parish politics, inheritance law, and the quiet violence of small communities.

chapters.title: The Will That Waits
chapters.summary: Ivo Fairweather, POV. A retainer arrives with a will dated for a death that hasn't occurred: the vicar of St. Aldhelm's, three days hence. The client, Edith Marsh, begs him to prove it a forgery before the anniversary dinner. Ivo recognizes his dead mentor's drafting hand in the document. Emotional beat: professional confidence curdling into unease as duty takes hold.

chapters.title: Parish Records
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, with interludes from Edith. He interviews the parish council and discovers the will names a beneficiary who officially died twenty years ago — the vicar's first wife. His mentor's old files reveal a suppressed inquest. Someone in the parish is watching Ivo's every move. Emotional beat: belonging fraying as the community he trusted closes ranks around him.

chapters.title: Anniversary Glass
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. At the anniversary dinner, staged as his trap, Ivo plants the forged will among the toasts and watches who flinches. The vicar's daughter, Ruth, poisons the wrong glass — Ivo's decoy — and is caught mid-act. She confesses her mother's murder was no accident, and the new will was her father's posthumous confession. Emotional beat: climax; love against duty shatters the parish's facade.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, weeks later. Ruth awaits trial; the vicar, dying, thanks Ivo for finishing what his mentor started. Edith withdraws her fee, ashamed of what the truth cost the parish. Ivo archives the case, barred from the community that made him. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — loyalty to truth honored, belonging forfeited, and Ivo at peace with the price.
